prompt: I run a Shopify store and I'm losing sales every time something sells out — shoppers see "Sold out" and leave without telling me they were interested. I want a "Notify me when back in stock" app so any shopper can leave their email on a sold-out item and hear from me the moment it's available again, and I can see in the admin which products people are waiting on so I know what to restock. Shoppers should sign up at the variant level when a product has multiple variants like sizes or colors (they pick the exact one and only get notified about that one), or at the product level when there's nothing meaningful to choose between — default to whichever fits. The widget sits on the product page right under the sold-out button, takes an email, confirms inline, and never appears on items already in stock. When something is back, every shopper waiting should be emailed in the order they signed up; if only a few units come back and many are waiting, notify the front of the queue and keep the rest for the next restock, and each shopper hears about a given item once per restock so no duplicate blasts if stock briefly dips. In the admin I want a dashboard ranking products by waitlist size, a drill-in to see individual subscribers and export them as CSV, an editor for the email subject and body (with product name, item details, and a one-click unsubscribe link), and quiet hours so nothing sends late at night. Every email needs a working unsubscribe that clears the shopper from all their waitlists; deleted products clear their waitlist cleanly; duplicate signups for the same item from the same email are a no-op; the same email across many products is fine. The number I care about most is "lost demand recovered" — how many signed up, how many got notified, and how many of those actually bought that item within a week.

intent.desiredOutcome: Capture lost demand from sold-out shoppers, automatically notify them on restock, and give merchants visibility into waitlist demand to inform restocking decisions.
intent.qualityBrief: A polished back-in-stock notifier handles: duplicate signups from the same email on the same variant (idempotent), partial restocks where fewer units arrive than waitlisted shoppers (queue fairly, notify only the front of the line, preserve the rest for the next restock), product deletions (clear waitlists cleanly without orphaned records), one notification per restock per shopper per variant (no duplicate blasts if stock briefly dips), guest email signups (no customer account required), and variant-level vs product-level logic (default intelligently based on variant count). The widget must never appear on in-stock items and must confirm inline without a page refresh. Merchants need run history in the admin, CSV export with proper escaping, a functional email template editor with preview, quiet-hours queueing that respects the setting, and accurate attribution of purchases back to notification sends (within 7 days).

plan.dataFlow: When a shopper visits a sold-out product page, the widget calls the backend to check current signup state and renders the email-capture form if the item is out of stock; the shopper submits their email and the backend records a signup (idempotent on email + variant). When Shopify fires variants/in_stock the backend creates a notification run for that variant, selects the front of the signup queue up to the available-unit count, enqueues notification sends for those signups, and leaves the remainder for the next restock. A schedule running every 5 minutes picks up enqueued sends that fall outside quiet hours and delivers each email, marking the send as dispatched; sends within quiet hours are held until the window opens. When an orders/paid event arrives the backend checks whether any dispatched send for the purchasing email and a matching variant is within the 7-day attribution window and records a conversion event. When products/delete fires, all waitlist signups and pending sends for that product are soft-deleted so no orphaned records remain. Merchants view the demand dashboard and drill-down from the admin panel, which reads from pre-aggregated waitlist snapshot and send-history tables.

triggers.event: a variant becomes back in stock
triggers.idempotency: if a notification run already exists for this variant external id and is in the current restock cycle (created after the last out-of-stock timestamp), treat the event as a no-op and do not create another run

triggers.event: a variant goes out of stock
triggers.idempotency: update the last-out-of-stock timestamp on the variant availability record; duplicate deliveries are safe because the write is idempotent
deletion is idempotent; if the product is already marked deleted, skip
if a conversion event already exists for this order external id, treat the event as a no-op

triggers.jobPurpose: Deliver queued back-in-stock notification emails that fall within the merchant's permitted sending hours.
triggers.perTickWork: Select up to a configurable batch of notification sends in enqueued status whose scheduled time is in the past and that fall within quiet-hours bounds, deliver each email, and mark each send as dispatched or failed.

capabilities.description: Return whether a given variant (or product) is currently out of stock and whether the requesting email is already signed up, so the widget renders correctly on page load.

Send the back-in-stock email for one queued send using the merchant's configured subject and body template, then mark the send as dispatched.
Mark a notification send as failed and record the reason when email delivery is rejected.

Remove a shopper from all their active waitlist signups via a one-click unsubscribe token, preventing any further emails.

Stream a properly-escaped CSV of all active subscribers for a given variant for merchant download.

edgeCases: Duplicate variants/in_stock delivery for the same restock cycle — checked against variant_availability.last_out_of_stock_at: if a notification run already exists with created_at after that timestamp, the event is a no-op with no run or sends created.

Partial restock where available units are fewer than active signups — only the front of the FIFO queue (up to available_units count) is enqueued; remaining active signups retain their position for the next restock cycle.

Stock briefly dips then recovers without a variants/out_of_stock event firing in between — the state machine invariant blocks a second notification run unless a genuine out_of_stock transition was recorded between runs.
Product deleted while sends are enqueued — purge-product-waitlists marks all signups as purged and cancels all enqueued sends so the schedule job skips them; the notification run is marked cancelled.
Email delivery fails on dispatch — the send is marked failed with the reason; the signup remains active so the shopper is eligible for the next restock cycle.

Shopper uses unsubscribe link — all active signups for that unsubscribe token's email are marked unsubscribed; subsequent schedule ticks skip those sends and future signup attempts via the widget are still permitted (new opt-in).
Duplicate orders/paid delivery for the same order — conversion_events keyed by order_external_id + send_id makes the write idempotent; the second delivery exits before any counter increment.

Quiet-hours window spans midnight (e.g. 22:00–07:00) — the scheduler must handle wrap-around correctly; sends created during quiet hours are held with status held_quiet_hours and released on the first tick after quiet_hours_end.

hld_v_findings.issue: The `dispatch-notifications` capability sends emails with a "one-click unsubscribe link". An unsubscribe link embedded in an email is opened by the recipient's browser, which issues a GET request. The only declared unsubscribe route is `POST /widget/unsubscribe` — there is no GET counterpart. A browser clicking the emailed link will receive a 405 Method Not Allowed; every unsubscribe in production is silently broken.
hld_v_findings.fix: Add a `GET /widget/unsubscribe` route to `externalContracts` with `requestShape: {"unsubscribe_token": "text"}` that accepts the token as a query parameter and delegates to the `unsubscribe-shopper` capability; the POST variant can remain for programmatic use but the GET is what the emailed link must resolve to.

hld_v_findings.issue: `product_title` and `variant_title` are persisted columns whose values are owned by Shopify. Per the external-state completeness rule, every column reflecting external system state must be bound to a trigger that refreshes it, fetched on demand, or declared as known-stale in an edge case. The plan has no `products/update` trigger, no on-demand fetch, and no edge case acknowledging that these titles go stale when a merchant renames a product or variant. The admin dashboard will silently display wrong product names with no plan path to correct them.
hld_v_findings.fix: Add a `products/update` external-event trigger (signalField: "product title", "variant titles", "product external id") with a corresponding capability that refreshes `product_title` and `variant_title` in `demand_snapshots`; alternatively, remove both columns from `demand_snapshots` and resolve the display names from Shopify at read-time in the `list-demand-dashboard` capability.

hld_v_findings.issue: `keyedByColumns` is empty, meaning no database-level uniqueness guard exists on `restock_runs`. The plan's one-run-per-item dedup relies entirely on an application-level check for an existing open/dispatching run. Under concurrent webhook delivery (two simultaneous `inventory_levels/update` events for the same item), the check-then-insert is a race condition: both handlers read no open run, both insert, and the item's shoppers are double-notified — the exact scenario the merchant cited as a critical quality requirement.
hld_v_findings.fix: Add a partial unique constraint (expressible as a `keyedByColumns`-equivalent) such as `["item_key", "status"]` scoped to active statuses, or introduce a dedicated `active_run_locks` table with `keyedByColumns: ["item_key"]` whose insert acts as the atomic gate; document the chosen concurrency strategy in the restock_runs `queryPatterns`.

hld_v_findings.issue: `dataNeeds` includes `"variant external id"` but the resolved `shopifySteps` op (`product`) is queried by `product external id` alone and returns all variants — the variant external id is not consumed by the Shopify call. Per spec, dataNeeds are inputs the capability requires to do its work; listing a value the capability receives but does not pass to its integration step is misleading and will confuse the coding agent about which argument to thread.
hld_v_findings.fix: Remove `"variant external id"` from `check-item-availability.dataNeeds`; if the widget needs it to pre-select a variant in the response, document that the frontend supplies it as a UI selection rather than as an input to the Shopify query.
